etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin immigrans, present active participle of immigrāre (“to migrate into”), from in- (“into”) +‎ migrāre (“to migrate”).

definitions.definition: A non-native person who comes to a country from another country to permanently settle there.

quote.citation: 1964, John F. Kennedy, A Nation of Immigrants‎[1], Revised and Enlarged edition, Harper & Row, →LCCN, →OCLC, page 2:
quote.text: What Alexis de Tocqueville saw in America was a society of immigrants, each of whom had begun life anew, on an equal footing. This was the secret of America: a nation of people with the fresh memory of old traditions who dared to explore new frontiers, people eager to build lives for themselves in a spacious society that did not restrict their freedom of choice and action.

quote.citation: 1980, AA Book of British Villages, Drive Publications Ltd, page 178, about Eynsford:
quote.text: The village was once well known for its paper-milling, founded by Huguenot immigrants in 1648, which produced high-quality hand-made paper until 1952.

quote.citation: 2019 July 15, Greg Afinogenov, “The Jewish Case for Open Borders”, in Jewish Currents‎[2], number Summer 2019:
quote.text: [Stephen] Miller’s uncle, a neuroscientist, has been welcomed onto the public stage for his denunciations of his nephew’s immigration policies, which the elder Miller has characterized as hypocritical: the Millers’ not-so-distant Jewish ancestors were, of course, immigrants themselves.

definitions.definition: A plant or animal that establishes itself in an area where it previously did not exist.
Of or relating to immigrants or the act of immigrating.
